title: Advanced Gerund & Infinitive Patterns: Prepositions, Adjectives & Complex Forms
grammarTitle: Advanced Patterns: Prepositions + Gerund, It + Adj + to-inf, Complex Forms
grammarNote: Помимо глаголов с изменением значения, на B1+ уровне важны три другие системы: 1) Герундий после предлогов (всегда!), 2) Конструкция it + adjective + to-infinitive, 3) Сложные формы: пассивный герундий, перфектный герундий, и need + герундий. Эти конструкции появляются в каждом академическом тексте.

grammarTable.subject: It + adj + to-inf
grammarTable.example: "It is DIFFICULT TO OVERSTATE." / "It is ESSENTIAL TO ACKNOWLEDGE." ✅

grammarTable.subject: Passive gerund
grammarTable.example: "Being denied access was frustrating." / "I hate being ignored." ✅

grammarTable.subject: Perfect gerund
grammarTable.example: "Having finished the report, she relaxed." / "I regret not having applied." ✅

grammarTable.subject: Passive perfect inf.
grammarTable.example: "She appeared to have been promoted." / "The results seem to have been misread." ✅

grammarTable.subject: Need + gerund
grammarTable.example: "The report needs updating." = "The report needs to be updated." ✅

grammarExtra.title: Prepositions ALWAYS followed by gerund — the critical rule

rows.example: "In addition TO CONSIDERING X, the study also examines Y." ✅ (NOT "to consider")
"Without ACKNOWLEDGING the limitations, this analysis is incomplete." ✅
"Instead of MEMORISING rules, try understanding the system." ✅
"As a result of HAVING REVIEWED the literature, the gap became clear." ✅
"Before SUBMITTING the essay..." / "After REVIEWING the data..." ✅
"I look forward TO SEEING you." ✅ NOT "to see" — TO here is a PREPOSITION! ✅

grammarExtra.title: It + be + adjective + to-infinitive — evaluative claims

rows.example: "It is ESSENTIAL TO ACKNOWLEDGE the limitations." ✅
"It is DIFFICULT TO OVERSTATE the significance of this." ✅

rows.form: It would be premature/wrong TO DO
rows.example: "It would be PREMATURE TO CONCLUDE that X is true." ✅
"It is POSSIBLE TO INTERPRET this finding differently." ✅
"It is HARD TO IMAGINE a world without digital communication." ✅

rows.form: Never use gerund: ✗ "It is important considering"
rows.example: ✅ "It is important TO CONSIDER." — always infinitive in this structure. ✅
"HAVING SUBMITTED the assignment, she felt relieved." (completed before the result) ✅
"I regret NOT HAVING applied earlier." (earlier non-action, now regret) ✅
"BEING IGNORED is frustrating." (being the object of ignoring) ✅
"She was upset at BEING TOLD to rewrite the essay." ✅
"She hates BEING INTERRUPTED." / "He doesn't mind BEING ASKED questions." ✅

grammarExtra.title: Need + gerund and complex infinitive structures

rows.form: Need + gerund = need to be done
rows.example: "The essay needs EDITING." = "The essay needs TO BE EDITED." — same meaning, less formal. ✅
"She seems TO HAVE BEEN SELECTED for the prize." (passive + perfect + infinitive) ✅
"She was happy TO HAVE BEEN CHOSEN." / "He was sorry TO HAVE MISSED the event." ✅
"The essay is TOO LONG TO READ in one sitting." / "She's TOO TIRED TO THINK clearly." ✅
"She's SMART ENOUGH TO UNDERSTAND the concept." / "Is it GOOD ENOUGH TO PASS?" ✅

rows.form: ✗ "In addition to study X, we also..."
rows.example: ✅ "In addition to STUDYING X, we also..." — preposition "to" → gerund. ✅
✅ "It is important TO CONSIDER..." — "It + adj + to-inf" structure always. ✅

rows.form: ✗ "She hates to be interrupted." (not wrong, but less natural)
rows.example: ✅ "She hates BEING INTERRUPTED." — gerund is more natural after hate/mind/like for states. ✅
✅ "Look forward to SEEING you." — "to" = preposition → gerund! ✅

grammarTip:
Advanced Gerund/Infinitive patterns:

PREPOSITIONS + GERUND (always!):
"In addition to STUDYING..."
"Without CONSIDERING..."
"Before SUBMITTING..."
⚠️ "Look forward TO SEEING" — TO = preposition here!

IT + ADJECTIVE + TO-INFINITIVE:
"It is important TO CONSIDER."
"It is difficult TO OVERSTATE."
"It would be premature TO CONCLUDE."
→ NEVER gerund: ✗ "It is important considering"

PERFECT GERUND (having + pp):
"Having FINISHED the report, she relaxed."
"I regret not HAVING APPLIED earlier."

PASSIVE GERUND (being + pp):
"Being IGNORED is frustrating."
"She hates being INTERRUPTED."

NEED + GERUND = need to be done:
"The report needs UPDATING" = needs to be updated.

TOO + adj + to-inf:
"Too tired TO THINK."
Adj + enough + to-inf:
"Smart enough TO UNDERSTAND."

exercises.text: "In addition to ___ (research) the topic, she also interviewed experts."
exercises.hint: "In addition TO RESEARCHING the topic." — preposition "to" → gerund. ✅

exercises.text: "I look forward to ___ (hear) from you soon."
exercises.hint: "Look forward TO HEARING from you." — "to" = preposition → GERUND. NOT infinitive "to hear." ✅

exercises.text: "It is ___ (essential) ___ (acknowledge) the limitations of the study."
exercises.hint: "It is ESSENTIAL TO ACKNOWLEDGE the limitations." — it + adj + to-infinitive. ✅
"She doesn't mind BEING ASKED difficult questions." — passive gerund (she = the one being asked). ✅

exercises.text: "___ (finish) the assignment, he felt a great sense of relief."
exercises.hint: "HAVING FINISHED the assignment, he felt relieved." — perfect gerund for completed action before the result. ✅

exercises.text: "The essay ___ (need) before we can submit it." (less formal)
opts: Both "needs revising" and "needs to be revised" work
exercises.correct: Both "needs revising" and "needs to be revised" work
exercises.hint: "needs REVISING" (informal) = "needs TO BE REVISED" (formal) — same meaning. ✅
"TOO COMPLEX TO UNDERSTAND without a dictionary." — too + adjective + to-infinitive. ✅
"EXPERIENCED ENOUGH TO MANAGE the project independently." — adjective + enough + to-infinitive. ✅
"The report appears TO HAVE BEEN MISINTERPRETED." — passive perfect infinitive. ✅

exercises.text: "___ (without / consider) the ethical implications, this research cannot be approved."
exercises.hint: "Without CONSIDERING the ethical implications." — preposition + gerund. ✅

exercises.text: "It is important considering all the evidence before drawing conclusions."
opts: "considering" should be "to consider" — it + adj + to-infinitive
exercises.correct: "considering" should be "to consider" — it + adj + to-infinitive
exercises.hint: ✅ "It is important TO CONSIDER all the evidence." NEVER gerund in this structure. ✅

exercises.text: "I regret ___ (not / apply) for the scholarship three years ago."
opts: Both "not applying" and "not having applied" work
exercises.correct: Both "not applying" and "not having applied" work
exercises.hint: "Not APPLYING" ✅ / "Not HAVING APPLIED" ✅ — both express regret about a past non-action. ✅

exercises.text: "___ (before / submit) the final report, all data must be verified."
exercises.hint: "BEFORE SUBMITTING the report." — preposition "before" + gerund. ✅ ("before we submit" with subject is also correct but different structure).
"She was delighted TO HAVE BEEN OFFERED the position." — passive perfect infinitive after adjective. ✅

exercises.text: "It would be ___ (premature) ___ (draw) conclusions from this data alone."
exercises.hint: "It would be PREMATURE TO DRAW conclusions from this data alone." — it + adj + to-inf. ✅

exercises.text: "Instead of ___ (memorise) vocabulary lists, focus on understanding words in context."
exercises.hint: "Instead of MEMORISING vocabulary lists." — preposition + gerund. ✅

questions.text: After ALL prepositions, which form must follow?
questions.hint: ALL prepositions (in, on, for, to, without, before, after, etc.) are followed by GERUND. ✅
"look forward TO" — "to" = PREPOSITION here → must use GERUND "seeing." ✅

questions.text: "It is difficult to overstate the importance of X." — "to overstate" because:
opts: "It + adj + to-inf" structure always uses infinitive
questions.correct: "It + adj + to-inf" structure always uses infinitive
questions.hint: "It is difficult TO OVERSTATE." — It + adjective + TO-INFINITIVE structure. Always infinitive. ✅

questions.text: "Having finished the report, she relaxed." — "Having finished" is:
questions.hint: "Having finished" = PERFECT GERUND (having + past participle). Completed action before the result. ✅

opts: Passive gerund (subject = the one being ignored)
questions.correct: Passive gerund (subject = the one being ignored)
questions.hint: "Being IGNORED" = passive gerund. The speaker is the recipient of the ignoring. ✅

questions.text: "The chapter needs rewriting." — What does this mean?
opts: Someone needs to rewrite the chapter for us
The chapter needs to be rewritten
questions.correct: The chapter needs to be rewritten
questions.hint: "needs + gerund" = "needs + to be + pp." Same meaning, less formal. ✅

questions.text: "It is important considering all the evidence." — Error:
opts: "considering" should be "to consider" — it + adj + to-infinitive structure
questions.correct: "considering" should be "to consider" — it + adj + to-infinitive structure
questions.hint: ✅ "It is important TO CONSIDER all the evidence." — NEVER gerund after "it + adj." ✅

questions.text: "The results appear to have been misinterpreted." — "to have been" is:
questions.hint: "to have been misinterpreted" = passive perfect infinitive. ✅

questions.text: "She was happy to have been selected." — The structure:
"Too complex to understand" vs "complex enough to understand":
opts: "Too complex" = impossible/difficult; "complex enough" = at the right level of difficulty to be worth understanding
questions.correct: "Too complex" = impossible/difficult; "complex enough" = at the right level of difficulty to be worth understanding
questions.hint: "TOO complex TO understand" = so complex you can't understand. "COMPLEX ENOUGH TO be worth analysing" = appropriate complexity. ✅

questions.text: "Without considering the implications, the approach is flawed." — "considering" because:

opts: "Without considering the costs, this plan is incomplete."
questions.correct: "Without considering the costs, this plan is incomplete."
questions.hint: "Without CONSIDERING the costs" — preposition + gerund. ✅ All others have errors.
